questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Snowflake Data Clean Room?

options.text: To physically copy data between two accounts for backup
To share data while controlling exactly which queries can be run against it, without giving unrestricted access
To replicate an account to another region
To monetize data on the public Marketplace

explanation.correct: A clean room lets a provider share data while defining what analyses/queries can be run against it, so consumers gain insights without unrestricted access to the underlying data.

distractors.A: Clean rooms do not copy data for backup; data is accessed only through approved templates.
distractors.C: Cross-region replication is a separate feature, not a clean room.
distractors.D: Clean rooms do not support monetization features.

questions.stem: In a Data Clean Room, how is a collaborator classified as a provider or a consumer?

options.text: By the Snowflake role they hold
By whether their account created the clean room (provider) or was invited to it (consumer)
By the size of their warehouse
By their Snowflake edition

explanation.correct: A provider is the account that created a clean room; a consumer is the account that was invited to (shared) the clean room. The role applies at the account level, not per user.

distractors.A: Provider/consumer status is not determined by Snowflake roles.
distractors.C: Warehouse size is irrelevant to clean room role.
distractors.D: Edition does not determine provider/consumer classification.

questions.stem: How is access to a Snowflake Data Clean Room obtained?

options.text: By searching and self-joining on the Marketplace
Automatically for all accounts in the region
By purchasing a listing
By invitation only from the clean room provider

explanation.correct: Access to a clean room is by invitation only; you must be invited by a clean room provider to access it.

distractors.A: Clean rooms are not self-joined via Marketplace search.
distractors.B: Access is not automatic; it requires an invitation.
distractors.C: Clean room access is by invitation, not by purchasing a listing.

questions.stem: Which THREE statements about clean room templates are correct? (Select THREE)

options.text: Consumers can run arbitrary ad-hoc SQL against provider data by default
Templates require no approval from the other party
A template is a JinjaSQL query installed in the clean room
By default, only consumers can run a template in a clean room
A template usually includes run-time parameters (e.g., columns or WHERE filters)
Templates cannot include any parameters

explanation.correct: A template is a JinjaSQL query installed in the clean room; by default only consumers can run templates; and templates typically include run-time parameters like column names or WHERE-clause filters.

distractors.A: You cannot run arbitrary SQL by default; usage is limited to approved templates unless the provider grants that ability.
distractors.B: A template must be approved by the other party to be used.

questions.stem: Which TWO data-protection controls can be configured in a Snowflake Data Clean Room? (Select TWO)

options.text: Automatic monetization of query results
Differential privacy
Specifying which columns are joinable or projectable
Granting consumers OWNERSHIP of provider tables
Disabling all access controls for faster queries

explanation.correct: Clean rooms let collaborators configure data-protection settings such as differential privacy and specifying joinable and projectable columns.

distractors.A: Clean rooms don't support monetization features.
distractors.D: Consumers never receive OWNERSHIP of provider tables in a clean room.
distractors.E: Clean rooms enforce access controls; they are not disabled.

questions.scenario: A company wants to install the Snowflake Data Clean Rooms environment for use across their whole account.
questions.stem: Who installs it and at what scope?

options.text: Each user installs it individually
It is installed once per clean room
An ACCOUNTADMIN installs it once for the entire Snowflake account
Snowflake Support installs it per warehouse

explanation.correct: The clean room environment is installed once for an entire Snowflake account (not per user or per clean room) by someone with ACCOUNTADMIN privileges.

distractors.A: It is not installed per user.
distractors.B: It is not installed per clean room; it is per account.
distractors.D: It is installed by an account administrator, not per warehouse by Support.

questions.scenario: In a standard clean room, a consumer runs an approved template against combined provider and consumer data.
questions.stem: Can either party directly view or query the other party's imported raw data?

options.text: Yes; the provider can view all consumer data
Yes; the consumer can browse provider tables freely
Only the provider can view both parties' data
No; imported data cannot be queried or viewed directly and is only accessed through templates

explanation.correct: Data imported into a clean room cannot be queried or viewed directly by either party; it can only be accessed through a template in the clean room.

distractors.A: The provider cannot directly view consumer data.
distractors.B: The consumer cannot browse provider tables directly.
distractors.C: Neither party can directly view the other's raw data.

questions.scenario: A provider wants to run one of their own queries against the consumer's data in a clean room.
questions.stem: What is required?

options.text: Nothing; providers can always query consumer data
The provider must request permission, and the consumer must consent to that specific query
The provider must recreate the clean room
The consumer must transfer ownership of the data

explanation.correct: By default only the consumer can run queries. If enabled, a provider can request permission from the consumer to run a specific query in the clean room, and the consumer must consent.

distractors.A: Providers cannot always query consumer data; it requires consumer consent.
distractors.C: Recreating the clean room is unnecessary and not the mechanism.
distractors.D: No ownership transfer occurs; consent to a specific query is what's needed.

questions.scenario: A team plans to convert an existing sharing arrangement or offer data more broadly, comparing sharing mechanisms.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about sharing mechanisms are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A direct share can auto-fulfill across clouds automatically
Listings cannot include any additional metadata
You can convert a direct share with active consumers to a listing
A Data Exchange lets you manage a group of accounts you invite to provide and/or consume
Direct shares can be offered publicly on the Marketplace

explanation.correct: You can convert a direct share with active consumers to a listing, and a Data Exchange lets you set up and manage a group of invited accounts that can provide and/or consume data.

distractors.A: Direct shares do not auto-fulfill across clouds; that is a listing capability.
distractors.B: Listings can include metadata such as title, description, and usage examples.
distractors.E: Public Marketplace offering is a listing capability, not a direct share.

questions.scenario: A provider shares live, read-only data with a partner who does NOT use Snowflake and wants to avoid ETL pipelines, data duplication, and manual exports.
questions.stem: Which Snowflake capability is designed for this?

options.text: Time Travel
Zero-copy cloning
Open Data Sharing
Fail-safe

explanation.correct: Open Data Sharing expands sharing beyond the Snowflake ecosystem, letting you securely share live, read-only data with consumers who don't use Snowflake, without ETL pipelines, duplication, or manual file exports.

distractors.A: Time Travel accesses historical data within a retention period; it is not for external sharing.
distractors.B: Zero-copy cloning duplicates objects within an account, not external sharing.
distractors.D: Fail-safe is a data recovery service, unrelated to external sharing.

questions.scenario: Two teams use the same Snowflake account to access clean room cleanroom1, which was created in that account and shared with account XYZ.
questions.stem: What clean room role do users in the creating account have?

options.text: They are all consumers for cleanroom1
Some are providers and some are consumers
They have no role until individually assigned
They are all providers for cleanroom1

explanation.correct: The provider/consumer role applies at the account level. All users in the account that created a clean room are providers for it; all users in an account it was shared with are consumers.

distractors.A: The creating account's users are providers, not consumers.
distractors.B: Roles are account-level and uniform, not mixed within an account for the same clean room.
distractors.C: Roles are determined by whether the account created or was shared the clean room, not per-user assignment.

questions.scenario: A clean room provider wants to invite users in the same account where the clean room was created to act as consumers.
questions.stem: A clean room provider considers who can be a consumer. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Any user in the creating account can be a consumer if they use a different warehouse
You cannot invite someone in the same account where you created the clean room to be a consumer
Provider/consumer roles apply at the Snowflake account level, not per user
Holding SAMOOHA_APP_ROLE lets a same-account user act as a consumer
Consumers are determined by their Snowflake role, not their account

explanation.correct: You cannot invite someone in the same account where you created the clean room to act as a consumer, and provider/consumer roles apply at the account level (not per user).

distractors.A: Warehouse choice does not change the account-level role restriction.
distractors.D: SAMOOHA_APP_ROLE grants API access, not same-account consumer status.
distractors.E: Roles are determined by whether the account created or was shared the clean room, not by Snowflake role.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about clean room access are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: The API can perform clean room account administration tasks
The clean rooms UI is accessed at the same URL as Snowsight
To use the API, a user must be granted the SAMOOHA_APP_ROLE by a clean rooms administrator
The clean rooms UI uses the user's Snowflake credentials
Anyone can use the clean rooms UI without being granted access

explanation.correct: API access requires being granted SAMOOHA_APP_ROLE by a clean rooms administrator, and the clean rooms UI uses your Snowflake credentials.

distractors.A: The API doesn't enable clean room account administration; that must be done in the UI.
distractors.B: The clean rooms UI is accessed at a separate URL from Snowsight.
distractors.E: You must be granted access to use the clean rooms UI by an administrator.

questions.scenario: A provider allows query results in a clean room to be exported to their own Snowflake account or a Snowflake-approved third party like an ads platform.
questions.stem: What is this exporting of results outside the clean room called?

options.text: Replication
Activation
Fulfillment
Provisioning

explanation.correct: When query results are exported outside the clean room, this is called activation. Results can be activated to a Snowflake account or a Snowflake-approved third party, always subject to approval by all parties who shared the data.

distractors.A: Replication is a business-continuity feature, not clean room result export.
distractors.C: Cross-cloud auto-fulfillment applies to listings, not clean room result export.
distractors.D: Provisioning is not the term for exporting clean room results.

questions.scenario: A provider wants to share a tag along with a tagged object so a consumer can see the tag assignments on shared objects.
questions.stem: A provider shares a tag with a tagged object. Which TWO statements about sharing tags are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: The provider grants OWNERSHIP on the tag to the share
The provider grants READ on the tag to make it available to the consumer
Sharing a tag requires MODIFY on the tag
The provider must create the tag in the same database as the tagged objects and share that database
Tags cannot be shared with consumers at all

explanation.correct: To share a tag, the provider grants READ on the tag (plus USAGE on the database/schema) and must create the tag in the same database as the tagged objects and share that database.

distractors.A: OWNERSHIP is not granted to the share to expose a tag; READ is.
distractors.C: MODIFY is not required to share a tag.
distractors.E: Tags can be shared with consumers via READ on the tag.

questions.scenario: A consumer wants to view shared tag references on objects the provider shared.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about shared tags on the consumer side are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: The consumer can view shared tags in Snowsight
The consumer can use the Account Usage TAG_REFERENCES view to see shared tags
Shared tags are read-only; the consumer cannot set a shared tag on their own objects
A role with IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the shared database can view the shared tags
The consumer can modify the provider's shared tag values

explanation.correct: Shared tags are read-only (the consumer cannot set them on their own objects), and a role with IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the database created from the share can view the shared tags.

distractors.A: Currently, the consumer cannot use Snowsight to view shared tags.
distractors.B: The Account Usage TAG_REFERENCES view cannot be used in the consumer account for shared tags.
distractors.E: Shared tags are read-only; the consumer cannot modify them.

questions.scenario: A provider sets a tag on a shared schema in a shared database and relies on tag inheritance.
questions.stem: What can the consumer see regarding where the tag was initially set?

options.text: The consumer can determine the exact level where the provider set the tag
Snowflake hides the LEVEL column values to protect the provider, so the consumer cannot see where the tag was initially set
The consumer sees the full tag lineage including the provider's account
Tag inheritance does not apply to shared databases

explanation.correct: Tag inheritance applies to shared objects, but the consumer cannot use TAG_REFERENCES to see where the provider initially set the tag; Snowflake hides the LEVEL column values to protect the provider.

distractors.A: The consumer cannot determine the exact level where the tag was set.
distractors.C: Snowflake does not reveal the provider's initial tag location/lineage to the consumer.
distractors.D: Tag inheritance does apply to tagged objects in the shared database.

questions.scenario: A consumer receives a share built with database roles (Option 1) and needs to give their analysts access to a shared database role.
questions.stem: What does the consumer do?

options.text: Grant OWNERSHIP of the shared objects to the analysts
Ask the provider to add each analyst to the share
Grant each shared database role to one or more of their own account roles
Nothing; database roles auto-grant to all users

explanation.correct: After creating a database from a share that includes database roles, consumers grant each shared database role to one or more account roles in their own account to give users access.

distractors.A: Consumers never get OWNERSHIP of shared objects.
distractors.B: The provider adds accounts, not individual analysts; access within the consumer account is managed by the consumer.
distractors.D: Database roles do not auto-grant to all users; they must be granted to account roles.

questions.scenario: A clean room provider configures optional variations beyond the standard clean room flow.
questions.stem: Which THREE variations can a provider permit in a clean room? (Select THREE)

options.text: Allow the provider to run their own queries against consumer data (with consent)
Allow query results to be activated (exported) to an approved destination
Grant the consumer OWNERSHIP of the provider's raw data
Allow either party to include custom Python code callable by the query
Automatically publish the clean room on the public Marketplace
Disable all approval requirements for data export

explanation.correct: Providers can permit variations such as running their own queries against consumer data (with consent), activating/exporting results to approved destinations, and including custom Python code callable by the query.

distractors.C: Consumers never receive OWNERSHIP of provider raw data in a clean room.
distractors.E: Clean rooms are invitation-only and don't support Marketplace publishing/monetization.
distractors.F: Exporting data outside the clean room is always subject to approval by all parties who shared the data.

questions.scenario: An administrator runs SHOW ROLES LIKE 'SAMOOHA_APP_ROLE'; and the role appears in the results.
questions.stem: What does this most likely indicate?

options.text: The account has exceeded its reader account limit
Replication is enabled for the account
A direct share is active
The clean rooms environment (API) is probably installed in the account

explanation.correct: If SHOW ROLES LIKE 'SAMOOHA_APP_ROLE' returns the role, the clean rooms environment (API) is probably installed in the account. SAMOOHA_APP_ROLE is required to use the clean rooms API.

distractors.A: The role's presence has nothing to do with reader account limits.
distractors.B: It does not indicate replication status.
distractors.C: It does not indicate an active direct share.
